_source: Transcribed from the GWMS Curriculum Guide in Notion, rebuilt September 26, 2026 for the three-games model. Game fields (games array) come from each session's Grappling Class Guide (Unit 7), Start 1 of each of the three CVP games, with the GWMS Game Rulings applied. TLO/ELO/connection/takeaway come from each session's Lesson and Intervention Guide. Nothing here is authored beyond plain-language rewording of the guides' own words.

stage.name: The Return
stage.grapplingTlo: By the end of the Return, participants will apply and integrate back-pin control and finishing, holding total control without harm, and analyze the distance traveled since Session 1.
stage.caselTlo: By the end of the Return, participants will apply responsible decision-making to name what changed, contribute to others, set a standard for who comes next, and choose what to carry forward, analyzing the cost and worth of those choices.
stage.connection: Total control, plus the choice not to hurt someone, is the heart of the whole program. Now you carry that choice out the door.

wrongAnswers.text: Holding the finish after your partner taps
wrongAnswers.feedback: Let go the instant he taps.

wrongAnswers.text: Hurting your partner because you can
wrongAnswers.feedback: That is the one thing you never do.

sessions.probingQuestion: What's actually different in you now?

games.title: Consecutive Touches Game
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, fighting for set touch points on the elbows named by the coach before the round.
games.text: Make two touches in a row on the set points, and stop your partner from doing the same.

win.role: Whoever makes two touches in a row first
win.text: wins. The same rule applies to both players.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is touching the same elbow spot twice.

games.title: Feet-Off Guard Passing Game
games.start: The bottom player is belly up in open guard. The top player is in front of him, hands already on him.
games.text: Top player: keep his feet off by clearing them and closing distance, stepping inside the knees or around the outside. Bottom player: use hooks, feet on the body, and posts to make the top player hit his butt or hands, then sit up with your back off the mat.

win.text: wins by touching his shin to the bottom player's body, inside or outside his knees.
wins by making the top player fall on his butt, then getting his own back off the mat.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is passing the legs from on top.

games.title: Back Take – Maintain Chest to Back Contact
games.start: The attacker is in full back control, chest on the defender's back, arms around the shoulders, hooks in. The defender may move freely.
games.text: Attacker: keep chest-to-back contact by following the defender wherever he goes. If your hands separate, reconnect them. If a hook comes out, put it back in. Defender: fight the connections to put your back on the mat or turn to face the attacker.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps contact.
wins by getting his back to the mat or turning face to face.

games.reset: The attacker holds no matter what. If the defender gets his back down or turns to face him, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is holding his back from behind.

sessions.connection: Twelve weeks ago, you could not hold this position at all. Now you can. That is proof of change you can feel. Naming what is different in you works the same way. Real change is something you can show, not just say.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, open guard, and back control. At Session 1 you could not hold these positions. Now you can. That is proof of change you can feel in your body, not just say out loud. You get to name exactly what changed and show it.

concept.lesson: Following through, not reaching for more too soon, proves change is real.
concept.question: Tonight you followed him wherever he went, standing, passing, and holding his back. What proved the change was real?

options.text: Following through instead of reaching for more.
options.feedback: Following through, instead of reaching for more too soon, is proof the change is real.

options.text: Reaching for more the first chance you got.
options.feedback: Reaching for more too soon is not the same as following through.

options.text: Holding on only when it was easy.
options.feedback: Holding on only when easy is not proof of anything.

sessions.probingQuestion: How do you know the change is real and not just talk?

games.title: Single Leg Takedown to Hip Connection Game
games.start: Both players stand. The attacker holds one of the defender's legs, somewhere from knee to ankle.
games.text: Attacker: move the defender, work out to the ankle, and use foot-to-foot contact to put him down on his hips or hands. Defender: free the leg, then grab one of the attacker's legs, knee to ankle.

win.text: wins when the defender is down on his own hips or hands.
wins by freeing his own leg and then grabbing one of the attacker's legs.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is a takedown to one leg.

games.title: Post and Hook Continuous Connection Game
games.start: The top player is standing. The bottom player is belly up with hooks on the top player's body and both hands on his ankles.
games.text: Top player: clear both feet to the outside for shin-to-body contact, or lock your hands from hips to shoulders. Bottom player: keep at least one hook and one hand connected at all times, using only posts and hooks to keep putting the top player on his butt or hands.

win.text: wins by getting outside the bottom player's legs for shin contact, or locking his hands at the bottom player's hips.
holds as long as he keeps his connections.

games.reset: The bottom player holds no matter what. If the top player breaks free and connects, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is staying attached with hands and feet.

games.title: Chest to Back Control Game
games.start: The top player is behind the bottom player with chest-to-back contact, both arms and both legs connected.
games.text: Top player: keep chest-to-back contact by following the bottom player and keeping your hands connected. Bottom player: put your back on the mat or turn to face.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps contact.
wins by getting his back to the mat or turning face to face.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player gets his back down or turns to face him, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is holding his back from behind.

sessions.connection: A change that only works when it is easy is not a real change yet. Holding the back against a fighting partner puts it to the test. Who you have become gets proven the same way, by whether it holds up when things get hard.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from a single leg, open guard, and back control. A change that's only easy isn't real yet, and holding the back against a fighting partner tests it. Who you've become gets tested the same way, when things get hard. You get to trust it once it holds.

concept.lesson: Change that only holds when it's easy isn't real yet.
concept.question: Tonight you held on standing, passing, and on his back, against someone really trying. What proved it?

options.text: It held even when he fought hard.
options.feedback: Real change holds up against real effort, not just when it's easy.

options.text: It worked when he wasn't trying very hard.
options.feedback: Working only when he's not trying is not proof of anything.

options.text: You said it, and that was enough.
options.feedback: Saying it is real does not make it real.

sessions.probingQuestion: What can you do now that the old you couldn't?

games.title: Underhook to Head, Waist, or Leg with Hip-Centric Win
games.start: Both players stand. The underhook player has an underhook. The overhook player has an overhook.
games.text: Underhook player: move your partner and connect with closed hands to the head, waist, or leg. A direct waist connection wins right away. Overhook player: use the overhook, your free hand, and your head to keep him away from those spots.

win.text: wins by connecting to the overhook player's waist, directly or from his head or leg.
wins by freeing a head or leg connection before the underhook player reaches his hips.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is locking his waist with an underhook.

games.title: Half Guard Opening Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his back in knee-shield half guard, both legs on one of the top player's legs. The top player's hands are on the bottom player's body.
games.text: Top player: hold the bottom player on his back, press on his hips, knees, and feet, then stand up, clear the feet, and touch your shin from knee to head on both sides. Bottom player: use hooks and posts to keep his feet off, making him hit his butt and sit up, or getting to closed guard.

win.text: wins by standing and touching both outsides of the bottom player's legs.
wins by putting the top player on his butt and sitting up, or by getting to closed guard.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is freeing a trapped leg to pass.

games.title: Chest-to-Back Position Maintenance
games.start: The top player is behind the bottom player, chest to back, with no hooks in.
games.text: Top player: follow the bottom player as he moves, keeping chest contact and staying under at least one elbow. If the position slips, go to chest-to-chest and keep contact. Bottom player: get both legs back in front in any guard, reverse the top player, or stand up.

win.text: wins by keeping control through the round.
wins by guard recovery, reversal, or standing.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is staying stuck to his back, turning.

sessions.connection: There is one exact thing you can do on the mat now that you could not before, and you can name it. Your growth off the mat works the same way. Not "I am better," but "I can do this now."
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from an underhook tie, half guard, and back control. There is one exact thing you can do now that you couldn't before, and you can name it. Growth off the mat works the same way. You get to name exactly what you gained.

concept.lesson: Growth is one exact thing you can name.
concept.question: Tonight you held on standing, passing, and on his back, with less help than before. What exactly changed?

options.text: One exact thing you can name, not just a feeling.
options.feedback: Growth is one exact thing you can name, not a feeling of being better.

options.text: A general feeling that you got better.
options.feedback: A feeling is not the same as naming one exact thing.

options.text: Something you can't quite describe yet.
options.feedback: If you can't name it yet, you haven't found it yet.

games.title: Upper vs Lower Body Division Game — Open Hand Connections
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range. One is the upper body player, one is the lower body player. Open hands only.
games.text: Upper body player: stay between, outside, or under your partner's arms. Get an underhook, or make his hands touch the mat. You may not touch his legs. Lower body player: touch only the head, hands, and elbows to move them, then touch anywhere behind the leg. You may not go under the arms. Whoever gets there first wins, then you switch roles.

win.text: wins with an underhook on the lower body player, or by putting his hands on the mat.
wins with a touch behind the upper body player's leg, or by putting his hands on the mat.

games.reset: Whoever wins goes first next time, and you switch jobs, the upper body player becoming the lower body player. Then you run it again.
games.whatItIs: This is fighting for upper body or legs.

games.title: Seated Open Guard Game
games.start: The top player stands. The bottom player sits on the mat with an inside hook and a knee-pit grip.
games.text: Bottom player: move from seated to belly up, using your connections to put the top player down on his hips or hands, then wrestle up or stand and make his back touch the mat. Top player: put the bottom player on his back and keep shin contact.

win.text: wins by standing up to grab the top player's hips, or by putting the top player's back on the mat and standing.
wins by touching his shin to the bottom player's knees or body.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is knocking a standing man down, sitting.

games.title: Back Take – Maintain Chest to Back Contact
games.start: The attacker is in full back control, chest on the defender's back, arms around the shoulders, hooks in. The defender may move freely.
games.text: Attacker: keep chest-to-back contact by following the defender wherever he goes. If your hands separate, reconnect them. If a hook comes out, put it back in. Defender: fight the connections to put your back on the mat or turn to face the attacker.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps contact.
wins by getting his back to the mat or turning face to face.

games.reset: The attacker holds no matter what. If the defender gets his back down or turns to face him, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is holding his back from behind.

sessions.connection: Helping a newer partner instead of just tapping them out is the first act of giving on the mat. Turning your growth toward someone who needs it works the same way in life. You stop being the one who gets helped. You start being the help.
sessions.note: Not everyone is ready to give yet. That is okay. Nothing here is owed.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, open guard, and back control. Helping a newer partner instead of tapping him out is the first act of giving on the mat. Turning what you've learned toward someone who needs it works the same way. You get to decide when you're ready.

concept.lesson: Holding someone so he can learn is giving, not winning.
concept.question: Tonight you held him standing, passing, and pinning, so he could learn. What made that giving?

options.text: You held him so he could learn, not to win.
options.feedback: Holding someone so he can learn is giving, not winning.

options.text: You held him hard.
options.feedback: Holding as hard as possible is winning, not giving.

options.text: You let him go early.
options.feedback: Letting him go skips the struggle he needs.

sessions.probingQuestion: What can you give that actually costs you something?

games.title: Front Headlock to Rear - Standing
games.start: Both players stand. The attacker has a standing front headlock, chosen before the round.
games.text: Attacker: use the shoulder connection to put the defender's hands on the mat, then find a path behind and lock your hands around his hips. Once behind, knee-block to put his hands on the mat, or lift both his feet off the ground. Defender: at any point, break every connection, stand fully, and turn to face the attacker.

win.text: wins by putting the defender's hands on the mat, and lifting him once from behind on his hips.
wins by fully disconnecting, standing, and turning to face.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is getting behind someone bent over.

games.title: Open Guard Multiple Connection Game
games.start: The top player stands, fully connected. The bottom player has inside hooks and a knee-pit grip.
games.text: Bottom player: stay connected, or get the connection back if it slips. Use it to put the top player on his butt or hands, then stand up and make his back touch the mat. Top player: put the bottom player on his back and fight to the knee pit or the outside, staying on your feet.

win.text: wins by putting him down and standing, or by wrestling up to a connection.
wins by touching his shin to the bottom player's knee pit, or his body from outside the legs.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is knocking a standing partner down.

games.title: Back Control Elbow Management — No Hooks
games.start: The front player sits in front. The back player sits behind him with no hooks, hands on the front player's hands but not connected to each other.
games.text: Back player: stay behind and under the front player's elbows, turning him toward the mat and keeping him facing it as long as you can, with no hooks and no hand lock. Front player: turn to face the back player and get both elbows free, by any method.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps control.
wins by turning to face the back player with both elbows free.

games.reset: The back player holds no matter what. If the front player faces him with elbows free, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is staying behind someone, arms only.

sessions.connection: Letting a partner work when you could just finish them costs you the easy win. Giving something real off the mat costs something too, time, comfort, pride. The giving that counts is the kind you feel.
sessions.note: Giving that costs you is not the same as erasing yourself. Giving until nothing is left of you is not the goal.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from a front headlock, open guard, and back control. Letting a partner keep working instead of finishing him costs you the easy win. Giving something real off the mat costs something too: time, comfort, pride. You get to choose what you give, without giving away everything.

concept.lesson: Giving up the easy win is what makes giving cost something.
concept.question: Tonight you gave him room to work, standing, passing, and on his back, while still holding on. What did that cost you?

options.text: The easy win you could have taken.
options.feedback: Giving up the easy win is what makes it cost something.

options.text: Nothing, holding on is always easy.
options.feedback: Holding on while giving him room is not the easy version.

options.text: Your grip, since you let go completely.
options.feedback: Letting go completely is not the same as giving him room while still holding.

sessions.probingQuestion: How do you use your strength without taking someone else's?

games.title: Foot-to-Foot Contact with Overhook / Underhook
games.start: Both players stand. The overhook player has an overhook. The underhook player has an underhook.
games.text: Overhook player: keep the overhook, use both hands to move your partner, and make foot-to-foot contact with either leg. Underhook player: close your hands anywhere below the overhook player's elbows and above his ankles.

win.text: wins when the underhook player falls onto his own hips or hands.
wins by closing his own hands under the overhook player's elbows.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is tripping him by blocking his foot.

games.title: Half Guard with Standing Transition Game
games.start: The bottom player is in half guard. The top player is on top with both knees on the mat, and may stand during the round.
games.text: Bottom player: while the top player is on his knees, work grips to get your feet inside and sit up. When he stands, shift to the legs, destabilize him, and get an entanglement. Top player: lock your hands anywhere from hips to shoulders, from your knees or from standing.

win.text: wins by getting his feet inside and sitting up, or entangling the top player once he stands.
wins by locking his hands.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.note: Wrestling up to the hips is not a win by itself. It is a path to the listed wins.
games.whatItIs: This is getting close to his back.

games.title: Chest to Back Control Game
games.start: The top player is behind the bottom player with chest-to-back contact, both arms and both legs connected.
games.text: Top player: keep chest-to-back contact by following the bottom player and keeping your hands connected. Bottom player: put your back on the mat or turn to face.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps contact.
wins by getting his back to the mat or turning face to face.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player gets his back down or turns to face him, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is holding his back from behind.

sessions.connection: You can have full control of someone's back and still choose not to hurt them. That is the whole system: the power to hurt, and the choice not to. Using your strength for people instead of over them is that same choice, made in your life.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from an underhook tie, half guard, and back control. You can control someone's back and still choose not to hurt him. That is the point. Using strength for people, not over them, is the same choice off the mat. You get to hold power and choose mercy.

concept.lesson: Choosing not to hurt him is what keeps strength from becoming harm.
concept.question: Tonight you had full control standing, passing, and on his back, and chose not to hurt him every time. What was that choice worth?

options.text: It kept your strength from becoming harm.
options.feedback: Choosing not to hurt him, every time you could have, is what keeps strength from becoming harm.

options.text: It proved you were stronger than him.
options.feedback: Proving you're stronger is not the same as choosing not to hurt him.

options.text: It made the round take longer.
options.feedback: How long the round took is not the point of the choice.

sessions.probingQuestion: What do you want to leave behind you here?

games.title: Hand Fight to Closed Hand Connection via Underhook
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, both disconnected.
games.text: Connect to your partner's wrist, elbow, and head, get the underhook, and fight to a closed-hand connection around the head, body, or leg.

win.text: wins. The same rule applies to both players.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is a hand fight that locks him.

games.title: Around-the-Legs Passing Game
games.start: The bottom player is belly up in open guard. The top player is on his feet, starting by clearing the feet.
games.text: Top player: get one leg outside the bottom player's feet, make shin contact from knee to head, then without stopping go around to the other side and touch there too. Bottom player: hook and post with your feet to make the top player hit his butt, then sit up with your back off the mat.

win.text: wins by touching one outside of the bottom player's legs, then the other outside, right after.
wins by making the top player fall on his butt, then getting his own back off the mat.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is getting around the legs.

games.title: Build to Rear Strangle Game
games.start: The top player is on the bottom player's back, hands connected, not yet in the finishing position. The bottom player may move freely.
games.text: Top player: first, get your over-grip palm to touch the bottom player's back. Once it touches, slide your wrist into the crook of your own other elbow and lock your hands. The win is the lock, not a squeeze. Bottom player: put your back on the mat, using any movement.

win.text: wins by touching the bottom player's back with his palm, then locking his own wrist into his other elbow.
wins when his back touches the mat.

games.reset: The win is the locked grip, not the finish. No finish is shown. The tap is honored instantly, every time. Roles switch after every win.
games.note: The win here is the locked grip, not the finish. No finish is demonstrated.
games.whatItIs: This is building a lock from behind, slowly.

sessions.connection: The finish is the sharpest power in the system. How you use it, controlled, releasing on the tap, is what people remember about rolling with you. What you leave behind in life is built the same way, out of how you treat people when you hold the power.
sessions.note: The jaw-based counters are not taught yet. They wait until the Therapeutic Manager approves them. Coaches do not teach them.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, open guard, and back control. A finish gives you real power. Letting go the second he taps is what people remember. Your legacy off the mat works the same way, built from how you treat people when you have the upper hand.

concept.lesson: A legacy is built step by step, with a controlled release.
concept.question: Tonight you built each position step by step, standing, passing, and finishing, and released on the tap every time. What does that leave behind?

options.text: A legacy built on control, not on seizing it.
options.feedback: What you leave behind is built from control, step by step, not from seizing the moment.

options.text: A legacy built on how fast you finished.
options.feedback: Speed is not what the legacy is built from.

options.text: A legacy nobody will actually remember.
options.feedback: What people remember is exactly how you built and released it.

sessions.probingQuestion: What standard are you setting for whoever comes next?

games.title: Single Leg Takedown Game
games.start: Both players stand. The attacker is connected to one of the defender's legs at the knee.
games.text: Attacker: move the defender and make him fall toward his hands or hips, running him, pulling him, turning him, or lifting him, using only that leg. Defender: stay balanced and use your connections to break the grip and free your leg.

win.text: wins when the defender touches the mat with his hips or hands.
wins by freeing his own leg from the attacker's grip.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is a takedown to one leg.

games.title: Guard Destabilization Game
games.start: The bottom player is on the bottom, feet between the top player's knees, one hand on his ankle. The top player stands.
games.text: Bottom player: use your feet and hands to pull the top player's hands to the mat above your head, and push or pull his butt to the mat too, both in the same rep, in any order. Top player: get to the outside of both legs and make shin-to-body contact.

win.text: wins when the top player's hands touch the mat above the bottom player's own head, and the top player's butt touches the mat too.
wins by getting outside the bottom player's legs and touching his body with a shin.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is tipping a standing player from below.

games.title: Chest to Back to Precursor Transitions Game
games.start: The top player is behind the bottom player with chest-to-back contact.
games.text: Top player: keep chest-to-back with your hands or hooks, or move to a precursor position on top, staying under an elbow while you move. Bottom player: put your back on the mat with nothing under your elbows, or turn face to face.

win.text: wins by reaching a precursor position on top.
wins by his back on the mat or by turning face to face.

games.reset: Chest to back is a continuous hold with no time count. He holds, and if the bottom player escapes, you reset. Reaching a precursor position on top is the other win. Roles switch after every win.
games.note: The win here is the precursor position, not the finish. No finish is demonstrated.
games.whatItIs: This is moving on his back to finish.

sessions.connection: How you carry yourself in the room, how you finish, how you treat a new partner, quietly sets the bar for everyone watching. The standard you set for whoever comes next in life works the same way. How you act is the standard.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from a single leg, open guard, and back control. How you act in the room quietly sets the standard for everyone watching. That is true on the mat and off it. You get to set that standard on purpose.

concept.lesson: What you do with a reached position quietly sets the standard.
concept.question: Tonight you reached a finishing position standing, passing, and on his back, and then chose what to do with it. What did that choice set?

options.text: The standard for whoever is watching you.
options.feedback: How you act once you're there sets the standard for whoever comes next.

options.text: Nothing, nobody was really watching.
options.feedback: Someone is always watching, even when it doesn't feel like it.

options.text: A standard only for this one round.
options.feedback: The standard you set does not stop at the end of one round.

sessions.probingQuestion: If someone watched how you carry yourself, what would they learn?

games.title: Hand Fight with Dual Win Conditions – Week 11 Game 1
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, both hand fighting at the wrists, elbows, and head.
games.text: Win one of two ways: collect three touches in any mix, or get an underhook and close your hands around your partner's shoulders, body, or leg.

win.text: wins, whether by three touches or by the underhook plus closed hands.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is fighting for touches or an underhook.

games.title: Closed Guard — Post to Underhook to Locked Hands
games.start: The bottom player has closed guard around the top player, who may work to standing.
games.text: Bottom player: attach to the wrists and elbows to cause a post, get the underhook on that post, then lock your hands around a shoulder. Top player: keep your hands on the bottom player and fight to stand up with the guard open.

win.text: wins by locking his hands with an underhook after a post.
wins by standing and opening the guard.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is catching an arm and locking hands.

games.title: Chest-to-Back Connection Maintenance
games.start: The top player is behind the bottom player, both hooks in, an under-over grip connected at the shoulders.
games.text: Top player: stay chest to back as long as you can, changing leg positions and upper-body grips as needed, without chasing finishes. Bottom player: get your back flat to the mat, or turn to face the top player and come on top.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps chest-to-back contact.
wins by getting his back flat to the mat, or by facing and coming on top.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player escapes, that is his win, and you switch to a new partner for the next round.
games.whatItIs: This is staying on someone's back.

sessions.connection: Newer people learn more from watching how you roll than from anything you say. How you carry yourself in life teaches the same way, silently, to whoever is watching. You are a lesson whether you mean to be or not.
sessions.note: This is about influence, not being watched and judged. Nobody is grading how you carry yourself.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, closed guard, and back control. Newer people learn more from watching how you roll than from anything you say. You teach people the same way off the mat, by how you act. You get to choose what you teach, since you're teaching anyway.

concept.lesson: Control without reaching for the finish teaches more than any finish.
concept.question: Tonight you held full control standing, passing, and on his back, without ever reaching for the finish. What did that teach whoever was watching?

options.text: That control, not the finish, is the lesson.
options.feedback: Control without reaching for the finish teaches more than any finish could.

options.text: That finishing fast is what matters most.
options.feedback: Finishing fast is not the lesson a newer partner actually needs.

options.text: Nothing, since you never finished anything.
options.feedback: Not finishing on purpose is still teaching something.

sessions.probingQuestion: What did this cost you, and what did you get for it?

games.title: 2v1 Hand Fight to Underhook to Close Hand Connection
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, both fully disconnected.
games.text: Get two connections on any two of your partner's wrist, elbow, or head, get the underhook, then go straight from there to closing both hands around his leg, body, or head.

win.text: wins. The same rule applies to both players.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is getting an underhook, then wrapping up.

games.title: Open Guard Takedown and Escape Game
games.start: The top player stands. The bottom player is on his back, fully connected, hands on the top player's ankles, feet inside his legs.
games.text: Bottom player: stay connected while putting the top player down on his hips or hands, then stand up, or stay connected as he rises. Top player: break the connections and make shin contact to pass.

win.text: wins by putting the top player down and standing up, or by rising up to a connection another way.
wins with shin contact.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is knocking a man down, then standing.

games.title: Chest to Back to Precursor Transitions Game
games.start: The top player is behind the bottom player with chest-to-back contact.
games.text: Top player: keep chest-to-back with your hands or hooks, or move to a precursor position on top, staying under an elbow while you move. Bottom player: put your back on the mat with nothing under your elbows, or turn face to face.

win.text: wins by reaching a precursor position on top.
wins by his back on the mat or by turning face to face.

games.reset: Chest to back is a continuous hold with no time count. He holds, and if the bottom player escapes, you reset. Reaching a precursor position on top is the other win. Roles switch after every win.
games.note: The win here is the precursor position, not the finish. No finish is demonstrated.
games.whatItIs: This is moving on his back to finish.

sessions.connection: Twelve weeks of getting tapped, cracked, and rebuilt cost something and gave something. Rolling now, you can feel both in your body. The honest ledger of what this cost and what you got is the first step of the return.
sessions.note: Grief and pride both belong here. Neither one cancels the other.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, open guard, and back control. Twelve weeks of getting tapped and rebuilt cost something, and gave something too. You feel both in your body when you roll now. You get to hold the cost and the gain together, without losing either one.

concept.lesson: Playing both seats means feeling the cost and the gain at once.
concept.question: Tonight you played both seats, standing, passing, and on his back, full rounds, every time. What did playing both seats let you feel?

options.text: Both the cost and the gain, at once.
options.feedback: Playing both seats lets you feel the cost and the gain at the same time, and both are real.

options.text: Only the gain, since you won most rounds.
options.feedback: Only feeling the gain misses half of what both seats teach.

options.text: Only the cost, since every round is hard.
options.feedback: Only feeling the cost misses the gain that came with it.

games.title: Hand Fight with Precondition Game
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, not gripped, starting to hand fight.
games.text: Collect three touches. A touch is a hand behind your partner's knee or an underhook. Any mix counts. Only after three touches can you try for a closed-hand connection.

win.role: Whoever collects three touches and then connects first
win.text: wins, closing his hands anywhere on his partner's body from shoulders to ankles.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is fighting to wrap him up.

games.title: Feet-Off Guard Passing Game
games.start: The bottom player is belly up in open guard. The top player is in front of him, hands already on him.
games.text: Top player: keep his feet off by clearing them and closing distance, stepping inside the knees or around the outside. Bottom player: use hooks, feet on the body, and posts to make the top player hit his butt or hands, then sit up with your back off the mat.

win.text: wins by touching his shin to the bottom player's body, inside or outside his knees.
wins by making the top player fall on his butt, then getting his own back off the mat.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is passing the legs from on top.

games.title: Build to Rear Strangle Game
games.start: The top player is on the bottom player's back, hands connected, not yet in the finishing position. The bottom player may move freely.
games.text: Top player: first, get your over-grip palm to touch the bottom player's back. Once it touches, slide your wrist into the crook of your own other elbow and lock your hands. The win is the lock, not a squeeze. Bottom player: put your back on the mat, using any movement.

win.text: wins by touching the bottom player's back with his palm, then locking his own wrist into his other elbow.
wins when his back touches the mat.

games.reset: The win is the locked grip, not the finish. No finish is shown. The tap is honored instantly, every time. Roles switch after every win.
games.note: The win here is the locked grip, not the finish. No finish is demonstrated.
games.whatItIs: This is building a lock from behind, slowly.

sessions.connection: The person rolling now is not the one who walked in on Session 1. You can see the difference in how you move. Naming who you became is the return itself, not who you were told to be, but the one you built.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, open guard, and back control. You are not who walked in on Session 1. You can see it in how you move. Naming who you became is the return itself. You get to claim that person, because you built him.

concept.lesson: Who you became was built and released on purpose.
concept.question: Tonight you built each position standing, passing, and finishing, and let go on the tap every time. What does that process say about who you became?

options.text: You built him and you released him on purpose.
options.feedback: Building something on purpose, then releasing it on purpose, is exactly how you became who you are.

options.text: He just happened to you over time.
options.feedback: Who you became did not just happen, you built him.

options.text: He is who you were told to be.
options.feedback: Who you became is who you built, not who you were told to be.

sessions.probingQuestion: What do you carry out this door?

games.title: Over-Under to Close Hand Connection
games.start: Both players stand in an even tie, one arm over and one arm under, on both sides.
games.text: Fight to get under your partner's elbows. Connect your hands anywhere from his armpits to his ankles.

win.text: wins by locking his hands around his partner's body, armpits to ankles.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is fighting to get an underhook.

games.title: Half Guard Side-Position Game
games.start: The bottom player is in half guard on his side, arms out straight. The top player is inside the half guard.
games.text: Top player: clear the bottom player's hands and get under at least one elbow, then connect your hands. Bottom player: keep your hands on the top player to deny that spot, and close your legs around his waist.

win.text: wins by getting under the bottom player's elbow and locking his own hands around him.
wins by closing his legs around the top player's waist.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is getting close while he blocks you.

games.title: Back Take – Maintain Chest to Back Contact
games.start: The attacker is in full back control, chest on the defender's back, arms around the shoulders, hooks in. The defender may move freely.
games.text: Attacker: keep chest-to-back contact by following the defender wherever he goes. If your hands separate, reconnect them. If a hook comes out, put it back in. Defender: fight the connections to put your back on the mat or turn to face the attacker.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps contact.
wins by getting his back to the mat or turning face to face.

games.reset: The attacker holds no matter what. If the defender gets his back down or turns to face him, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is holding his back from behind.

sessions.connection: The last roll ends, and then you walk out the door. What you carry out, control, mercy, the ability to stay, the real self, is the whole point. The mat was never the destination. What you carry out of it is.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the over-under tie, half guard, and back control, the three moves the whole program built toward. The mat was never the destination. What you carry out the door, control, mercy, the ability to stay, the real you, is the point. You get to carry it out.

concept.lesson: The games stayed the same. You are who changed.
concept.question: Tonight you played the same games as your very first night, standing, passing, and on his back. What was actually different this time?

options.text: Who was playing them, not the games themselves.
options.feedback: The games never changed. What you carry out the door is who was playing them.

options.text: The games were harder than before.
options.feedback: The games stayed the same, you were the one who changed.

options.text: Nothing, it felt exactly the same.
options.feedback: Something was different, even if the games looked the same.
